draft.title: The 68-95-99.7% rule
card: In a bell-shaped distribution, scores cluster around the mean. The 68-95-99.7% rule says how much of the data lies within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean.
About 68% of scores lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean. About 95% lie within 2, and about 99.7% lie within 3.
The distribution is symmetric, so the percentages split evenly either side of the mean. Within 1 standard deviation, about 34% lie on each side.

Example: test marks have mean 60 and standard deviation 10. Within 2 standard deviations means 40 to 80, so about 95% of marks are in that range. The other 5% are split evenly, so about 2.5% score above 80.
draft.remember: The 68-95-99.7% rule: within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean lie about 68%, 95% and 99.7%.

a.q: The masses of apples from an orchard are bell-shaped, with mean 150 g and standard deviation 10 g. About what percentage of apples have a mass between 130 g and 170 g?
a.why: 130 g and 170 g are each 20 g from the mean, which is 2 standard deviations. About 95% of values lie within 2 standard deviations. 68% is tempting, but that is the share within only 1 standard deviation, 140 g to 160 g.
a.clue: Find how many standard deviations 130 g is below the mean.

b.q: The times taken to travel to school are bell-shaped, with mean 30 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes. About what percentage of trips take more than 40 minutes?
b.why: 40 minutes is 2 standard deviations above the mean. About 95% of trips lie within 2 standard deviations, so about 5% lie outside, split evenly between the two ends. That gives 2.5% above 40 minutes. 5% is wrong because it counts both ends.
b.clue: The values outside the range are split evenly between both ends.
